## Teaching points

1. Examine the genitals of every male with lower abdominal or groin pain: torsion can present as abdominal pain, and here the scrotum was never examined.
2. Pain radiating to the scrotum, or a scrotum that hurts to touch, means torsion must be excluded with examination, urgent Doppler ultrasound or urology review, not only an appendicitis work-up.
3. Read the image margins: a 'whirl' sign of the spermatic cord at the inferior edge of an abdominopelvic CT suggests torsion.
4. Improvement after analgesia does not exclude torsion, and intermittent torsion can untwist and recur.
5. Salvage depends on ischemia time; after a delay of 2 days this testis was necrotic, and the contralateral testis was fixed because the predisposition is usually bilateral.
